assertions.text: Precision after verification is at least 0.8
assertions.how: a grader who has not seen the run maps each confirmed finding that is not a deterministic tool finding to one seeded defect, to 'real but not seeded' (with the reason it is a genuine problem for these users), or to 'not a problem'; precision = (seeded + real but not seeded) / confirmed judged findings >= 0.8. Also report the strict precision, seeded / confirmed judged findings, and the recall by meaning

assertions.text: The reply puts the fixes in priority order and says what needs a person
assertions.how: the final reply lists the confirmed problems from most to least severe, or the P0/P1 first, and names what the agent could not check (needs-human WCAG items, real skippers)

findings.title: Focus order jumps back: "Electric wet tile saw, 180 mm" → "Search tools"
findings.description: After "Electric wet tile saw, 180 mm", Tab moves to "Search tools", which sits 654 px above it in the same column; the focus order does not follow the visual reading order (clear-inversion heuristic).

findings.title: Focused element hidden behind body > div.actionbar: "One week"
findings.description: When "One week" receives focus (Tab), none of nine sample points on its box reaches it: body > div.actionbar (fixed) paints over it, so the focused element is not visible.

findings.title: Escape does not close the open loan-length list
findings.description: Expected (APG select-only combobox / listbox popup): Esc closes the open list and returns focus to the Loan length button. Current: after #loan-button opens #loan-list with Enter and ArrowDown moves to 'Two weeks', Esc leaves the list open with focus still on the option (probes/60 after-esc.png).

findings.title: Pick-up session radios are shown in reverse date order, but focus and arrow keys follow the DOM order
findings.description: Expected: focus order and reading order match the visual order (2.4.3, 1.3.2). Current: on /basket.html the six session radios appear newest first (Wednesday 28 October at the top or full width, then 24, 21, 17, 14, 10) at both 1280 px and 320 px. The DOM and accessibility tree list them oldest first (Saturday 10 October first). Tab from 'Remove' lands on Saturday 10 October, the last item on screen (bottom right at 1280 px, bottom at 320 px). ArrowDown then moves to Wednesday 14 October, which sits to its left or above it, so arrow navigation runs against the visual layout.

findings.title: Tool names are cut off with an ellipsis at 320 px, so the two cordless drills look identical
findings.description: Expected: at 320 CSS px, content reflows without loss of information (1.4.10). Current: the card title links on / are truncated to one line at 320 px ('Cordless drill 18 V, c...' twice, 'Extension ladder 3 ...', 'Pressure washer, 13...'). The words that tell the two drills apart (two batteries / one battery) are not visible. The scripted check reported horizontal overflow on the same cards; the truncation is a separate loss of content.

findings.title: Under forced colours at 320 px the dots that mark session days disappear from the calendar
findings.description: Expected (A11Y-22): meaningful indicators stay visible in forced-colours mode. Current: at 320 px the calendar marks session days only with a small green dot (the 'Open' text is hidden at this width). With forced-colors: active the dots are not drawn, so session days look the same as every other day. The selected day keeps a visible border and bold number.

findings.title: Tool-card and basket-item headings sit at the same level as the 'Tools' section heading that contains them
findings.description: Expected (A11Y-26): the heading outline mirrors the structure, so headings nested in a section sit one level below its heading. Current: on / every card title is an h2 inside region 'Tools', whose own heading is also h2. On /basket.html the basket item 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' is an h2 under h2 'Tools'. Elsewhere the outline is sound: one h1 per page and no skipped levels.

findings.title: 'Reserve this tool' action bar and the 'Added to your basket' status sit outside every landmark
findings.description: Expected (A11Y-26): all content sits inside landmarks. Current: on /tool.html the fixed action bar with the primary 'Reserve this tool' button and the role=status toast are siblings of main and contentinfo, outside both.

findings.title: Pick-up day chosen on the tool page must be matched again with a session in the basket
findings.description: Expected (recognition rather than recall; no re-entry within a process): a choice already made carries forward. Current: the member chooses 'Pick-up day: Saturday 17 October' on /tool.html, and the basket shows 'Pick up Saturday 17 October'. The 'Pick-up session' radio group still starts with nothing selected and fails with 'Choose a pick-up session' if Continue is pressed. The matching session (Saturday 17 October, 10:00 to 13:00) is one of six options, listed in reverse order (see a11y-02).

findings.title: Loan-length listbox has no Escape or outside-click close
findings.description: A popup listbox should close on Escape and return focus to its button, and close when focus or a click moves elsewhere. The handlers on #loan-button and #loan-list handle only click, Arrow, Tab, Enter and Space; there is no Escape branch and no document-level click or focusout handler, so the list stays open until an option is chosen or the button is clicked again.

findings.title: A search with no matches leaves the previous results on screen
findings.description: A search that matches nothing should say so and offer a way back. search() only re-renders and updates #results-status when the filtered list is non-empty; with zero matches it does nothing, so the earlier cards and the earlier 'N tools found' status remain, and no empty state exists in the markup.

findings.title: Continue and Confirm show no visible pending state during their delay
findings.description: Actions taking over a second should acknowledge the press at once. On submit, #continue (1.2 s) and #confirm (1.5 s) only receive aria-busy="true"; styles.css has no [aria-busy] or loading rule, the label does not change and the buttons stay enabled, so nothing on screen changes until navigation or an error.

findings.title: Repeat Confirm presses allocate extra reservation numbers
findings.description: A submit should create one reservation however often it is pressed while pending. The confirm submit handler pushes a new reference (FT-4471 + refs.length) into sessionStorage before its 1.5 s timeout, with no guard against a second submit; each extra press in that window adds another reference, and done.html then shows 'Reservation numbers FT-4471 and FT-4472' for the same tools and session.

findings.title: Ten-minute basket hold is never shown and cannot be extended
findings.description: A time limit on a task should be stated and adjustable or extendable. The hold starts when the first tool is reserved (HOLD_MINUTES = 10) and is checked only when Continue is pressed; no page shows the limit or the time left, and nothing warns before it expires or offers more time. The basket copy says only 'Items are held for you while you finish'.

findings.title: Expired-hold error reads 'Something went wrong. Try again.' and retrying fails the same way
findings.description: An error should name the cause and a way forward. When the hold has expired the basket shows 'Something went wrong. Try again.'; the hold start time is not reset by the error path, so every retry hits the same branch and shows the same message. Only done.html's 'Reserve another tool' clears hold_started.

findings.title: Closed library days are selectable as pick-up days
findings.description: Inputs should prevent choices that will be rejected. The tool-page calendar renders all 21 days as enabled buttons; closed days differ only by lacking the 'Open' tag or dot. Reserve accepts any day, and the closed day is rejected only after the member has filled in their details and pressed Confirm on the last step.

findings.title: Closed-day error on confirm gives no way to change the day
findings.description: Each error in a summary should lead to the place where it can be fixed. The closed-day errors are plain <li> text without links, and the basket page offers only Remove per tool, not a day change; the per-tool day can only be changed by going back to the tool page and reserving again.

findings.title: Card names are cut to one line, hiding the words that tell similar tools apart
findings.description: Names that distinguish items should stay readable. .card__name a forces white-space: nowrap with text-overflow: ellipsis. Below 768 px a card's text column is about 190-200 px, and 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and '... one battery' differ only at the end; their meta line and badge are also identical, so the two cards may render the same. No title or second line exposes the rest.

findings.title: Results grid's 330 px column minimum is wider than the content area at 320 px
findings.description: Content should reflow at 320 CSS px without horizontal scrolling. .results uses repeat(auto-fill, minmax(330px, 1fr)); with 16 px page padding each side the content area is 288 px at 320 px (328 px at 360 px), so the single column overflows the viewport.

findings.title: Fixed Reserve bar covers the footer's desk phone number at the end of the tool page
findings.description: .actionbar is position: fixed with min-height 72 px, but .page--bar reduces the bottom padding to 8 px, so after scrolling to the end of a tool page on a phone the footer's desk phone number stays under the bar.

findings.title: Dark-mode success colours differ from the declared tokens and leave the badge low in contrast
findings.description: Theme values should follow DESIGN.md. In dark mode DESIGN.md sets success #8fd1a8 and selection #24352c; styles.css sets --color-ok #2f7d4a and --color-ok-tint #1d2622 (the card surface). The 'Available from' badge text #2f7d4a on #1d2622 computes to about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text, and the badge background matches the card so it has no visible fill.

findings.title: Membership and phone fields reject common ways of writing valid values
findings.description: Validation should accept reasonable variants and normalise them. The membership check /^FT-\d{5}$/ rejects lower-case 'ft-01234' and a missing hyphen; the phone check /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/ rejects '+44 7700 900123', '07700 900 123' and hyphens. Values are only trimmed, not normalised.

findings.title: The three-tool limit stated on the find page is not enforced when reserving
findings.description: Stated rules should be enforced where the action happens. The find page says members can reserve up to three tools at a time, but the Reserve handler adds any tool with no count check, and basket and confirm also accept any number.

findings.title: After 'Reserve this tool' nothing says the reservation is unfinished or what to do next
findings.description: A first-time member who presses a button labelled 'Reserve this tool' needs to be told that the tool is only held and that a session and a confirmation are still needed, with a way to get there. Today the only feedback is a small toast 'Added to your basket'. It has no link and is gone within 5 s. The button label does not change. The header count changes to 'Basket (1)', but at that moment the header is scrolled off screen. The tool page offers no next-step prompt, so the only way forward is the small header link.

findings.title: On phones the search field sits below the whole tool catalogue
findings.description: Search should be available where a member looking for a specific tool starts. At 375 px the 'Search tools' field and the filter button come after all ten tool cards, about two and a half screen heights down the page. Nothing above the list mentions search.

findings.title: Sticky 'Reserve this tool' bar covers the pick-up day instruction on first view
findings.description: The page should make it clear, before the member acts, that a pick-up day is needed first. At 375 x 900 on load, the sticky 'Reserve this tool' bar sits over the paragraph 'Choose the day you will collect the tool. Days marked Open ... are library sessions.' The prominent bar is offered before the day is chosen. Pressing it shows 'Choose a pick-up day first.' above the calendar.

findings.title: Header still shows 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: After a successful confirmation, the page should not suggest that anything is still pending. The 'Reservation confirmed' page shows the reservation clearly, but the header link still reads 'Basket (1)'.

findings.title: Pick-up calendar accepts days that are not opening sessions
findings.description: Every day in the calendar is selectable: choosing Monday 12 October (not a session) and pressing Reserve adds the drill to the basket with 'Pick up Monday 12 October'. The closed day is only rejected later, on the confirm page.

findings.title: A tool can be reserved and confirmed for a day before it is available
findings.description: Choosing a pick-up day earlier than the tool's 'Available from' date is accepted all the way through: the pressure washer (available from Saturday 17 October) was reserved for Saturday 10 October and reached 'Reservation confirmed'; the sander ('Available from Wednesday 21 October') was accepted into the basket for Saturday 10 October.

findings.title: Basket and confirm accept a pick-up session that contradicts the chosen pick-up day
findings.description: The reservation summary should describe one collection time. After choosing Saturday 17 October on the tool page, choosing the Wednesday 28 October session in the basket proceeds without comment, and the confirm page then shows both 'pick up Saturday 17 October' under Tools and 'Wednesday 28 October, 18:00 to 20:00' under Pick-up session. The same contradiction appears after using Change to move to Wednesday 21 October.

findings.title: 'Reserve this tool' only adds the tool to a basket
findings.description: A button labelled 'Reserve this tool' should reserve it. Pressing it shows 'Added to your basket'; the reservation is made only after the basket and confirm steps. The label suggests the task is finished at this point.

findings.title: Continue and Confirm reservation show no response for about a second after pressing
findings.description: A press should be acknowledged within 0.1 s and work over 1 s should show progress. After 'Continue' in the basket the page is unchanged at 0.3 s and 0.7 s and moves to confirm between 0.7 s and 1.2 s; after 'Confirm reservation' nothing changes at 0.1 s and the done page appears within about 2 s. Neither button shows a pressed or busy state.

findings.title: Change from confirm returns to the basket with the chosen session cleared
findings.description: A member pressing 'Change' next to the session expects to see their current choice and adjust it. The basket opens with all six session radios unchecked, although Saturday 17 October was selected.

findings.title: Details typed on the confirm page are lost after using Change
findings.description: Leaving to change the session and coming back should keep what the member typed. After entering membership number and name, pressing Change, choosing a new session and continuing, the confirm page shows all three fields empty.

findings.title: On phones, search and the date filter sit below the full tool list
findings.description: At 1280 px Search tools and Filters appear above the list; at 375 px they come after all ten tool cards, near the footer. A member who wants to filter by day, and does not know where the filter is, has to scroll past the whole catalogue to find it, and after searching the results are above the field, out of view.

findings.title: Date filter hint says 'on or after this day' but the filter shows tools available by that day
findings.description: The filter labelled 'Available from' has the hint 'Show tools you could pick up on or after this day.' With 17 October entered, the sander (available Wednesday 21 October) and wet tile saw (Saturday 24 October) are removed, although both could be picked up after 17 October. The filter actually shows tools available on that day, which the label and hint do not say; the label also reuses the cards' own 'Available from' wording.

findings.title: On phones the fixed Reserve bar covers the footer's second line at the end of the tool page
findings.description: At 375 px, after scrolling to the end of a tool page, the second line of the footer (contact details) remains under the fixed 'Reserve this tool' bar and cannot be scrolled into view (probes/32 bottom.png).

findings.title: On phones, session days are marked only by a small dot that needs a written explanation
findings.description: At 375 px the 'Open' label of desktop is replaced by a small green dot under the date, and the meaning is only given in the paragraph above ('Days marked Open (a green dot on a small screen) are library sessions'). There is no legend at the calendar.

findings.title: Remove in the basket takes effect at once with no undo
findings.description: Removing a tool releases a hold on a one-of-a-kind item. 'Remove' deletes the tool from the basket immediately; there is no confirmation, no message naming what was removed and no way to undo. Restoring it means going back to the tool page and choosing the loan length and day again.

findings.title: Keyboard focus on a calendar day can sit hidden under the sticky Reserve bar
findings.description: The focused control should stay visible. At 1280 x 900, focusing Saturday 17 October and pressing Enter leaves the whole 11-17 October row, including the focused and selected day, behind the sticky 'Reserve this tool' bar.

findings.title: The date filter sits behind an unlabelled icon button
findings.description: The only way to see tools for a given day is the 'Available from' field, which appears only after pressing a button that shows a filter icon with no visible text (accessible name 'Filters'). The persona does not know where the date filter is. Nothing on the page mentions filtering by day.

findings.title: Each calendar day is a separate Tab stop
findings.description: The pick-up calendar puts all 21 day buttons in the Tab sequence and arrow keys do not move between them. From Loan length a keyboard user presses Tab 22 times to reach Reserve this tool.

findings.title: Loan length button is announced only by its value
findings.description: The Loan length control is a button whose accessible name is the current value ('One week'); the label 'Loan length' is only the heading of the surrounding region. Tabbing to it, a screen-reader user hears 'One week, button' without what it sets.

findings.title: Stale 'Choose a pick-up session' error stays after the basket is emptied
findings.description: After Continue fails and the member removes the only tool, the basket shows 'Your basket is empty' and, under it, the error box 'There is a problem: Choose a pick-up session', whose link points to a session list that is no longer on the page.

findings.title: Done page exposes the tool name twice to assistive technology
findings.description: In the reservation summary the Tools value is exposed as a list item and again as plain text, so a screen reader reads 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' twice. Visually it appears once.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench tile instead of the tool
findings.description: All ten cards on find use an identical wrench glyph in a pale-green square as the thumbnail. The thumbnail occupies about a fifth of each card and distinguishes nothing; it reads as a placeholder left in place.

findings.title: Tool names truncated at 375 so the two drills look identical
findings.description: At 375 tool names are cut with an ellipsis: both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…', and 'Extension ladder 3 m …', 'Pressure washer, 130 …' lose the spec that distinguishes them.

findings.title: Search and filters fall below the full tool list at 375
findings.description: On find at 375, 'Search tools', the Search button and the filter toggle appear after all ten cards, just above Opening times; at 768 and up they sit above the list.

findings.title: Sticky reserve bar cuts across the calendar and sits outside the content edge
findings.description: In the first viewport of the tool page the white action bar crosses the calendar (1280: through the first week row, clipping 'Open' under Sat 10; 375: over the Pick-up day help text). Its button ends at x≈1264 while all content ends at 1184.

findings.title: Details list uses two different label column widths
findings.description: On the tool page the Details list has Category/Deposit/Available from values at x≈224 and Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case values at x≈180, with an extra gap between the two groups.

findings.title: Basket session grid leaves one full-width row above five squeezed cards at 1280
findings.description: At 1280 the first session spans the full width while the other five sit in one row of narrow cards whose labels wrap to three lines.

findings.title: Pick-up sessions are listed latest date first
findings.description: The basket lists sessions from Wednesday 28 October down to Saturday 10 October, the reverse of calendar order, at every width.

findings.title: Dark theme inverts availability chip emphasis
findings.description: In dark mode the 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' chips show green text with almost no visible fill, while later-availability chips ('Sat 17 Oct', 'Wed 21 Oct') keep a visible grey fill.

findings.title: Filter labels 'Available from' and 'Category' are not aligned
findings.description: In the open filter panel the Category label and select sit lower than the Available from label and date field, so the pair looks misaligned.

findings.title: No-results state shows the full list and no message
findings.description: The no-results capture has 'sewing machine' in the search field but shows all ten tools with no empty-state message.

findings.title: Wide layouts on confirm and done leave the right half empty
findings.description: At 1280 the summary boxes span the full 1088px frame but the form fields, note and 'What happens next' box stop at ~610px, leaving a large empty area on the right.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name in bold body text
findings.description: The masthead is a small stroke wrench beside 'Fernhill Tool Library' in the body face; no screen carries anything of the library's world (the card, the desk, the shelves, the community centre).

findings.title: Navigation items wrap to two lines at 375
findings.description: At 375 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)', 'Opening / times' each break across two lines under the name.

findings.title: Membership number example breaks across lines in error text
findings.description: At 375 the inline error 'Enter your membership number, like FT-01234' breaks after 'FT-'.

findings.title: Filter Category select is unthemed while Loan length select is themed
findings.description: The Category select in the filter panel shows the native system chevron, unlike the themed Loan length select on the tool page.

findings.title: Filter labels 'Available from' and 'Category' are not aligned
findings.description: The Category label sits lower than the Available from label in the open filter panel.

findings.title: Done page gives no weight to the reservation number and leaves the viewport bare
findings.description: On done the reservation number FT-4471 is body text in a key-value row, the 'What happens next' box stops at half width, and the lower half of the 1280 viewport is empty ground. The nav still reads 'Basket (1)'.

findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench glyph as its thumbnail
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page use an identical wrench outline in a pale green square where a tool image would go. The slot reads as a placeholder, adds no information to tell a ladder from a pressure washer, and is the largest graphic element on the page. For members scanning for 'the drill with two batteries' on a phone, a picture or a tool-specific glyph would carry recognition; the repeated filler makes the page look unfinished.

findings.title: No signature or identity beyond the name in bold text
findings.description: Across find, tool, basket, confirm and done, the only identity is 'Fernhill Tool Library' set in bold body type beside a small icon. Ground, accent, type and card frame match the category default and fail the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests. The product's own world (the community-centre room, the membership card whose green is cited in DESIGN.md, the session rhythm of Saturday mornings and Wednesday evenings) is absent from the visuals.

findings.title: Tool names truncate with ellipsis at 375, making the two drills identical
findings.description: At 375 px card titles are cut to one line: both drills show 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', and 'Extension ladder 3 m ...', 'Pressure washer, 130 ...' lose the distinguishing spec. The distinguishing detail is exactly what members use ('the drill with two batteries'). Phones are the main device.

findings.title: Search field moves below all ten cards on phones
findings.description: At 1280 the search field sits above the grid; at 375 it appears after the tenth card, just above 'Opening times'. The page's job is 'find a tool', and on the main device the finding control is demoted below ~2,000 px of cards.

findings.title: Basket session cards: latest-first order and one oversized card above five cramped ones
findings.description: At 1280 the six sessions are listed from Wed 28 Oct back to Sat 10 Oct. The first card spans the whole row; the remaining five share a row and wrap to three lines each. The layout gives most weight to the least likely session and breaks the date-time strings awkwardly ('Saturday 24 / October, 10:00 to / 13:00').

findings.title: Tool details table uses two different label-column widths
findings.description: Category/Deposit/Available from align values at about x=224, while Chuck/Batteries/Weight/Case align at about x=180, so the values form two ragged columns in what reads as one table.

findings.title: Dark theme drops the chip background on green availability badges only
findings.description: In dark mode, 'Available from Sat 10 Oct' badges render as bare green text, while later-date badges ('Available from Sat 17 Oct', 'Wed 21 Oct', 'Sat 24 Oct') keep a grey chip. In light mode both kinds have chips. The dark theme reads as partly inverted rather than composed.

findings.title: Footer does not reach the bottom of short pages at 1280
findings.description: On basket and done at 1280x900 the footer ends above the viewport bottom and a band of bare page ground shows beneath it.

findings.title: Confirm form and done next-steps leave the right side of the container empty
findings.description: On confirm the form fields, and on done the 'What happens next' panel, occupy only the left half of the 1088 px container while the summary above spans the full width.

findings.title: Masthead navigation items wrap to two lines at 375
findings.description: At 375 'Find a / tool', 'Basket / (1)' and 'Opening / times' each break across two lines, with the active underline split.

findings.title: axe color-contrast: Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
findings.description: Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds (serious impact). Fix any of the following: Element has insufficient color contrast of 3.07 (foreground color: #2f7d4a, background color: #1d2622, font size: 12.0pt (16px), font weight: bold). Expected contrast ratio of 4.5:1

findings.title: Text contrast below 4.5:1: "Available from Sat 10 Oct"
findings.description: Text "Available from Sat 10 Oct" (16 px, weight 700) has 3.07:1 against its computed background in the dark theme at 320 px; it needs 4.5:1.

findings.title: Touch-primary controls closer than 8 px: "Saturday 17 October, open" and "Reserve this tool"
findings.description: On the 768 px touch viewport, the hit areas of these primary controls are 0 px apart (edge to edge); they need ≥ 8 px.

findings.title: Text clips under the text-spacing override in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: With line-height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em and word spacing 0.16em, text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") is cut off at 1280 px (scroll 427×50 vs client 390×50).

findings.title: Text clips at 200 % text size in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: With the root font size at 200 %, text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") is cut off at 1280 px.

findings.title: Overlapping text: #reserve
findings.description: At 1280 px, text of #reserve ("Reserve this tool") overlaps text of button.day:nth-of-type(9) > span.day__num ("17") by 16×14 px.

findings.title: Horizontal page overflow on /?items=ladder-3m
findings.description: scrollWidth 346 px > clientWidth 320 px at 320 px. Widest offender: #results > li:nth-of-type(1) extends 26 px past the viewport; 9 more.

findings.title: Content does not reflow at 320 px on /?items=ladder-3m
findings.description: scrollWidth 346 px > clientWidth 320 px at 320 px. Widest offender: #results > li:nth-of-type(1) extends 26 px past the viewport; 9 more.

findings.title: Clipped text in li:nth-of-type(1) > article.card > div.card__body > h2.card_
findings.description: Text ("Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries") overflows a box with overflow hidden at 320 px (scroll 327×46 vs client 184×46, axis x).

findings.title: Text overlaps under the text-spacing override: #reserve
findings.description: At 320 px with the WCAG 1.4.12 spacing override, #reserve ("Reserve this tool") overlaps #tool-from ("Saturday 10 October").

findings.title: Text overlaps at 200 % text size: #reserve
findings.description: At 320 px with the root font size at 200 %, #reserve ("Reserve this tool") overlaps #tool-blurb ("A brushless combi drill with hammer action, two 4 Ah batteri").

findings.title: Body text closer than 16 px to the viewport edge: "Cleaning · deposit £30"
findings.description: Text starts 145 px from the left and ends 9.7 px from the right edge of a 320 px viewport; body text needs ≥ 16 px at widths below 768 px.

findings.title: Cramped padding: "Pressure washer, 130 bar Cleaning · depo"
findings.description: Inside this bordered or filled container (17 px text): horizontal inset 6.4 px < 8.5 px.

findings.title: Not reachable by keyboard: "Fernhill Tool Library"
findings.description: The a "Fernhill Tool Library" is tabbable in the DOM, but a complete Tab walk never reached it. People who use a keyboard or switch cannot operate it.

ground_truth.description: At 480 px and below the stylesheet reorders the page so the list of tools comes before the search form, and the only way to the 'Available from' date and the category filter is an icon-only button (three lines) that opens a collapsed panel below the list. A member who wants tools for a given Saturday sees ten cards first and no date control, so they are unlikely to notice that filtering by day exists. The document order is form then results, so keyboard focus also runs against the visual order.

A search with no matching tool (for example 'sewing machine') leaves the previous results on the page and shows no message: the status region stays empty and the list does not change. The member cannot tell whether the search ran, whether nothing matched, or whether the old list is the answer.

Tool names are kept on one line and cut with an ellipsis inside the card's text column. At phone widths 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, two batteries' and 'Cordless drill 18 V, combi, one battery' both read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co…' (at 375 px; a character more or less at other widths), so a member cannot tell which card is the right one without opening each; only from about 480 px does the difference show. The full name is only in the link's hidden overflow.

In the dark theme the 'Available from' badge is a mid green (#2f7d4a) on the card surface (#1d2622), about 3.1:1 for 16 px bold text, below the 4.5:1 that text of that size needs; the light theme passes. Members who use dark mode on their phones get the availability line as the least legible text on the page.

The results grid asks for columns at least 330 px wide; at 320 px the content box is 288 px, so the cards run 42 px past it and the page scrolls sideways by 26 px. The same happens at 200% zoom on a 640 px window.

Every day in the calendar can be chosen, including the days the library is closed; only session days carry the word 'Open' (a green dot on a phone). Choosing a closed day highlights it and the page confirms 'Pick-up day: Monday 12 October'. The reservation is refused three steps later, on the confirm page ('The library is closed on Monday 12 October…'), and the only way back to the calendar is the browser.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' shows 'Added to your basket' for 1.2 seconds and nothing else changes nearby; the only lasting sign is the basket count in the header, which on a phone is above the fold. A member who looked away, or who reads slowly, does not know whether the press worked and presses again.

The 'Reserve this tool' bar is fixed to the bottom of the window and nothing keeps the page clear of it: the page ends 8 px under the calendar and the footer runs under the bar. A day button that sits in the bottom 72 px of the window counts as visible to the browser, so Tab reaches it without scrolling and the bar covers the focused control: at 768 px wide (900 px tall) the first two rows of days, at 1280 px the third row; on a phone the footer and the desk phone number sit under the bar at the end of the page.

The loan-length list opens as a custom listbox. Inside it, Tab moves to the next option and wraps around, and Escape does nothing, so a keyboard user cannot leave the list except by choosing an option with Enter.

The basket says 'Items are held for you while you finish' but shows no time; the hold is ten minutes from the first item and is kept only in the browser. When it has lapsed, Continue waits 1.2 seconds and then says 'Something went wrong. Try again.', which is not what happened and does not say what to do.

The pick-up sessions are laid out in reverse (row-reverse with reversed wrapping), so the earliest session appears last on screen, at the bottom of the stack on a phone and at the end of the row on a desktop, while coming first in the document. Tab moves from the rightmost card leftwards, against reading order, and a screen reader hears the sessions in an order a sighted member does not see.

'Confirm reservation' stays enabled while the request runs for 1.5 seconds, and nothing visible says that anything is happening. A second press, which is what people do when nothing seems to happen, allocates a second reservation number; the confirmation page then lists two reservations for one visit, and the desk holds the tool twice.

The 'Change' link beside the pick-up session returns to the basket without the chosen session, so a member who only wanted to look at the summary comes back to a basket with no session selected and has to choose again. Nothing says the choice was dropped.

The calendar neither marks nor disables the days before the tool's 'Available from' date, the basket offers every session, and confirm does not check: a wet tile saw available from Saturday 24 October reserved for Saturday 10 October ends on 'Reservation confirmed'. The member is told a tool will be waiting when it cannot be, and finds out at the desk.

Each tool keeps the pick-up day chosen on its tool page, the session is chosen separately in the basket, and nothing reconciles them: a drill to be picked up on Saturday 17 October can be confirmed for the Wednesday 21 session, the confirm page shows both dates and the done page only the session, so it is unclear which day the desk sets the tool aside for.

The loan-length button has no aria-label or aria-labelledby, so its accessible name is only its current value: a screen-reader user hears 'One week, button, collapsed' and is not told what is being chosen.

The membership number must match /^FT-\d{5}$/ and the mobile number /^0\d{4}\s?\d{6}$/, with no normalising: 'ft-01234', 'Ft-01234' (what a phone's sentence capitalisation makes of it) and 'FT 01234' are rejected, and so are '07700 900 123' and '+44 7700 900123', the form phone autofill often supplies. Each gets an error whose example looks like what the member typed.

After 'Reservation confirmed' the basket is not emptied: the header still reads 'Basket (1)' and the basket still lists the tool as held, and going back to the confirm page and confirming again reserves the same tool a second time under a new number.

Pressing 'Reserve this tool' with no day chosen shows 'Choose a pick-up day first.' in a paragraph with no role or live region that the calendar does not reference, so it is not announced, and focus moves to the first day button, a closed day before the tool is available. The message stays on screen after a day is chosen.

Below 480 px the word 'Open' on session days is hidden and an 8 px dot takes its place; what the dot means is only in the hint above the calendar. On the phone, the members' main device, which days the library opens is easy to miss. The seeder chose the dot to fit the calendar at phone widths; the second labeller and two reviews judged it a minor problem.

The find page says members may reserve up to three tools at a time, but the basket takes a fourth tool without a warning and the reservation is confirmed for four, so the desk has to turn the member away from some of them at collection.

With the membership number, name and mobile filled in, 'Change', the basket and Continue bring the member back to the confirm page with all three fields empty; the details are kept nowhere, so she types them again on a phone.

The tool page asked for a pick-up day and the basket line repeats it, yet no pick-up session is selected and Continue answers 'Choose a pick-up session', so the member enters the same date a second time, in another form, and can choose a different one.

On the done page the Tools entry holds the visible list item and a visually hidden span with the same name, so screen readers read the reserved tool's name twice; next to two reservation numbers this can sound like two tools.

The 'Available from' filter keeps the tools that can be collected on the chosen day, but its label uses the badges' words and its hint says 'Show tools you could pick up on or after this day': choosing 14 October hides a tool available from 17 October, which could be picked up after the 14th.

'Reserve this tool' does not reserve: it puts the tool in a basket held for ten minutes, the button keeps its label, and nothing says that a basket, a session and a confirmation still follow. A first-time member can believe the tool is reserved and put the phone down, and the hold lapses with nothing reserved. It is the press D07 describes, read for a different harm: D07 is the brief feedback, this is the misleading action.

I audited the reservation flow on all five pages (find, tool, basket, confirm, done) at six widths from 320 to 1440 px, in light and dark mode. It isn't ready for members yet, and most of what needs fixing hits phone and dark-mode users hardest.

**How it was checked.** I ran every automated check, and replayed both journeys. Three independent reviewers worked through the flow from different angles, and a persona walked the "reserve a tool for Saturday" journey on a 375 px phone. Three design critics, an accessibility auditor and a source-code reviewer also took part. Every candidate problem was re-checked on the live site, and three raters scored severity blind.

**Result.** The site reached no assurance level; your PRODUCT.md target is L3. It is blocked by WCAG and functional failures, 4 P0 and about 30 P1 findings, and the design panel's verdict. Nothing has been tested with real members yet. I didn't change any site files.

## Fix first (P0)

1. **The 10-minute basket hold is invisible, and when it runs out the reservation is stuck.** The basket only says "Items are held for you while you finish." There is no time shown, no warning and no way to extend. A verifier waited 10.3 minutes: Continue then showed "Something went wrong. Try again." and every retry showed the same error. Members reserving in the evening a few minutes at a time are the people most likely to hit this (`app.js:7`, `app.js:90-100`, `app.js:360-364`; also WCAG 2.2.1).
2. **The loan-length list traps the keyboard.** Once it is open, Escape doesn't close it. Tab only moves between "One week" and "Two weeks", so the calendar and "Reserve this tool" can't be reached (`app.js:238-251`). Its button is also announced only as "One week", not "Loan length".
3. **Focus order on the find page.** At tablet and desktop widths, the search box sits above the results but receives focus only after all ten tools. On phones, the search and filters sit below the whole catalogue (`styles.css:247-269`, `index.html:35-82`).

## Next (P1, grouped by cause)

4. **Collection time is asked twice, and the two answers can disagree.** The member picks a pick-up day on the tool page. The basket then asks for a pick-up session, doesn't pre-select it, and lists sessions latest date first. It also accepts a session that contradicts the day, so the confirm page shows two different dates.
5. **The calendar accepts days that don't work.** Closed days are only rejected on the last step, and that error offers no way to change the day. Days before the tool is available go all the way through to "Reservation confirmed": the pressure washer was booked for a date before it is available.
6. **"Reserve this tool" doesn't reserve.** It adds the tool to a basket and shows a toast for about 5 seconds. The walkthrough persona would stop there, believing the tool was reserved.
7. **Dark mode.** The green "Available from…" badge text measured 3.07:1, and WCAG AA needs 4.5:1. The dark success colours in `styles.css:60-61` don't match the values in DESIGN.md. In dark mode the unavailable chips also look stronger than the available ones.
8. **Tool names on phones are cut to one line.** Both drills read "Cordless drill 18 V, co…". At 320 px the results grid also overflows sideways because of a 330 px minimum column width. At 200% text size, both names and the Reserve bar clip or overlap (`styles.css:377`).
9. **The fixed Reserve bar has too little space under it.** On phones it covers the focused loan option, the pick-up instruction and the desk phone number in the footer (`styles.css:205`, `styles.css:758`).
10. **Smaller flow problems.** Pressing Confirm twice gives two reservation numbers. Continue and Confirm show nothing for about a second after being pressed. After confirming, the header still says "Basket (1)". A search with no matches shows the full list with no message. "ft-…" and "+44…" are rejected as invalid, with an "Enter your…" message.

The design panel judged the look *generic* and *plain*: every card has the same wrench tile, and the name is set in bold body text. That matters less than the items above.

## Keep these

- The error summaries on basket and confirm work well: they take focus, are announced, link to each field and keep what was typed.
- The done page says plainly what to bring and where to go.
- Deposits and "nothing is paid online" appear where people make decisions.
- The copy is in members' own words.

## Things to know

- **Duplicates in the report.** It lists 86 confirmed findings, but several are the same problem reported by different reviewers. For example, truncated names appear four times and "search below the list" four times. The groups are listed in the debrief, and the numbered list above is the de-duplicated view.
- **Inferred priorities.** You couldn't be asked during the run, so I prioritised for phones in dark mode, as your brief says. I treated nothing as off-limits to change.
- **Questions for members or the desk.** Does the green or grey badge colour mean anything the date doesn't? Do members think of "pick-up day" and "pick-up session" as the same thing?
- **Still needed for L3.** Someone needs to do real VoiceOver and TalkBack passes, test 200% zoom on a phone, and confirm the P0s.
- **One file edit.** One critic wrote a field in the wrong shape, which crashed the report generator. I wrapped that text in a list without changing its content.

Files are in `.ui-evaluator/runs/20261009-223234-audit-standard/`:
- `report.md` / `report.html`: the full report
- `debrief.md`: the synthesis, including the duplicate groups
- `agree-disagree.csv`: for you or volunteers to mark up
